findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice when shard splitting delegates to runSplitQuery
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables to each target, and the resulting sub-request is handed to runSplitQuery (line 163), which in querySplitting.ts (line 299) applies applyTemplateVariables again to every target. Every shard sub-request therefore goes through template/ad-hoc-filter interpolation twice (the updated test even asserts applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times for a single query). This can duplicate ad-hoc filters / label filters injected by applyTemplateVariables, re-interpolate values that themselves contain `$`-like text, and recompute `$__auto`/step against the already-substituted expression, producing incorrect queries. One of the two interpolation points should be removed (e.g. let runSplitQuery skip interpolation when called from shard splitting).

findings.title: runSplitQuery may re-interpolate already-interpolated targets from other callers
findings.body: runSplitQuery unconditionally calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on request.targets. Callers that already interpolate before calling runSplitQuery (shard splitting, and any datasource.query path that pre-processes targets) will now have variables/ad-hoc filters applied a second time. There is no guard or flag to opt out, so the function's contract silently changed: passing pre-interpolated targets is no longer safe. Consider adding an option (e.g. `skipInterpolation`) or documenting/enforcing that callers must pass raw targets.

findings.title: Assertion on interpolation call count codifies the double-interpolation behaviour
findings.body: The test was changed from expecting interpolation once to `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)`. That number is exactly 1 (shard splitting) + 4 (re-interpolation inside runSplitQuery per sub-request), i.e. the test now locks in the duplicate interpolation described above instead of verifying that each query is interpolated exactly once. If the duplication is fixed this assertion must change; as written it hides the defect.
